explanation: The pole grades: it fires on tokens inside a claim that places a referent on a ranked scale together with its comparison set - a superlative or ordinal with the set spelled out in the same clause ('the biggest plant we have operated', 'the most expensive plant we have operated', 'the largest of the four we operate', 'the fastest runner we had ever trained', 'more turrets than any other battleship'), or a rank, score or accolade noun standing inside such a passage ('Senior Professor of Bible Exposition', 'Bill Hunter Memorial Trophy', 'honorable mention', '将棋大賞', 'robust ranking results', a '9,8' review score, a 'generally positive' reception). The peak sits on the relative-clause subject or the clause comma that completes the comparison ('the biggest plant we have operated' peaks on ' we', 'the largest of the four we operate,' peaks on the comma); direction on the scale is irrelevant (smallest and worst fire like biggest), bare degree words with no set ('very large', 'extremely large', 'larger than the others') and the same rank nouns in a plain one-sentence frame ('he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics', 'she got a mention in the local paper', 'a bronze trophy at the flea market') stay under the active line, and a plain adjective plus relative clause still leaves roughly a quarter to a third of a superlative's peak; promotional self-reference ('Follow us on:', Indonesian 'hubungi kami') is the one other family it covers, and a few strong peaks (an IP address in code, a Japanese song title) remain unexplained.
